key_insight: Optimized curved rectangular vortex generators enhanced heat-exchanger performance, with separate designs improving the Colburn factor by 53.1%, area goodness factor by 14.4%, and volume goodness factor by 26.5%.
engineering_relevance: Tailoring vortex-generator geometry can improve water-to-air finned-tube heat exchangers while balancing heat-transfer gains against pressure-drop penalties.
method: Developed and validated a conjugate numerical model of a representative heat-exchanger section.
Used central composite experimental design and nonlinear polynomial regression to model four geometry parameters: attack angle, curvature angle, axial position, and height.
Applied a genetic algorithm to optimize heat-transfer-only and combined heat-transfer/friction objectives.
evidence_signal: Numerical comparisons against a plain-fin reference showed distinct optimized configurations achieving the reported gains; the abstract states model validation but provides no validation-error metrics.
watch_item: The reported gains belong to different objective-specific geometries and should not be assumed to occur simultaneously in one design.
paper_title: Optimization of curved vortex generator geometry for enhanced thermal performance in water-to-air finned-tube heat exchanger
